pr_title: net: ip: packet_socket: fixing raw sckt IPPROTO_RAW usage
pr_body:
net_packet_socket_input() was changed to hardcode the return of NET_CONTINUE and that caused a segmentation fault/crash in net_core/process_data(), in cases when pkt was unreferred and NET_OK was returned from net_conn_input().
This happened with socket combo of: AF_PACKET+SOCK_RAW+IPPROTO_RAW.
This PR includes a fix by ignoring only `NET_DROP` returns to allow also other layers to process the packet, and return `NET_OK/CONTINUE` as it used to.
Adding also, a new test case for testing related socket combo.

Fixes: #38516

issue_context.title: subsys: net: ip: packet_socket: always returning of NET_CONTINUE caused access to unreferred pkt and causing a crash/segmentation fault
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
net_packet_socket_input() was changed to hardcode the return of NET_CONTINUE and that caused a segmentation fault/crash in net_core/process_data(), in cases when pkt was unreferred and NET_OK was returned from net_conn_input().
This happens with socket combo of: AF_PACKET+SOCK_RAW+IPPROTO_RAW.

**To Reproduce**
Send and receive data with socket of combo: AF_PACKET+SOCK_RAW+IPPROTO_RAW.
I have also a new unit test case to reproduce the problem.

**Expected behavior**
Should not crash. I.e. net_packet_socket_input() cannot always override the verdict of the packet done by net_conn_input().

**Impact**
AF_PACKET+SOCK_RAW+IPPROTO_RAW sockets cannot be used. 

**Logs and console output**
New unit test case for reproducing the problem: https://github.com/jhirsi/zephyr/commit/82b83a5612d16058416f288ff22c35ae7a45c865

Or use modem_shell with ppp dial up with nrf9160 DK:
https://github.com/nrfconnect/sdk-nrf/tree/master/samples/nrf9160/modem_shell
and a crash occurs in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/net/ip/net_core.c#L119
when connecting and see the shell output.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
Unit tests.

**Additional context**

review_comments:
There might be a race condition, based on priorities, in case this thread has higher prio than the work thread. In such case the socket would be close before receive, IMO we should not itroduce such risky patterns even in tests.

It should be fine to do the other way - `recv()` here and call `sendto()` from the work. Or even simpler - just call `recv()` after `sendto()` directly from here - the packet should be bufferd in the net stack I believe?
Thanks for the comments. Simplified the test case to send/recv directly from here.
